about.title: Dana Point Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Dana Point draws visitors and residents alike to its harbor, coastal bluffs, and busy retail stretches along Pacific Coast Highway and Stonehill Drive. Wet tile near restaurant patios, uneven pavers outside beachfront shops, or poorly lit stairwells at hillside condos can all lead to a serious fall in an instant. California law doesn't make a property owner automatically responsible just because someone got hurt on their premises — you generally have to show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why documentation matters so much: photos of the spill or broken step, witness names, and especially surveillance footage before it gets erased. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm — we simply connect you with an independent attorney in the area who can evaluate what happened, gather that evidence, and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Dana Point Fall

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard — an attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so getting a preservation letter out quickly can make or break a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: Because California uses pure comparative fault, a property owner's insurer may try to pin partial blame on you — a lawyer can push back on that with the right evidence.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Dana Point?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California law. That window can be much shorter if the property involved is owned by a city, county, or other public entity, so it's worth having an attorney check this early. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to pursue a claim at all.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover even if you share some blame — your compensation is just reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help gather evidence to keep that percentage as low as possible. This is especially relevant on uneven walkways common near harbor-area shops and older sidewalks.

items.question: I fell at a store near PCH or Stonehill Drive — what should I do first?
items.answer: Take photos of exactly what caused the fall before it's cleaned up or fixed, and ask the business to preserve any surveillance footage in writing. Get the names of employees or witnesses nearby, and seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor at first. Then reach out so we can connect you with an attorney who can follow up on the property's history of complaints or prior incidents.
